title: Multi agent feature stream run
first_prompt:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<system-reminder>
<tools-used-before-summary>Ag

commits.summary: application-core values V1 step 1: the interpreter's Strings are UTF-16 code units, as the JVM's
commits.body:
The interpreter, which replays every witness, held a String as Rust UTF-8 text, so every isolated surrogate became U+FFFD: "\uD800".equals("\uFFFD") and "\uD800".equals("\uDC00") were true, charAt gave 65533, and a surrogate pair split by substring became two U+FFFD. Now interp::JStr holds a String's and a StringBuilder's code units, and every modelled operation works on them as the JDK's do: StringBuilder.reverse keeps a pair together, indexOf(int) takes a supplementary code point, strip and isBlank use Character.isWhitespace's set, new String(char[]) and its siblings are modelled, append(CharSequence, int, int) is refused instead of appending the whole sequence, and setLength(-1) throws. An operation that needs Unicode's tables (case conversion, equalsIgnoreCase, number syntax) is refused on a String with an isolated surrogate, and Integer.parseInt on any non-ASCII code unit (Character.digit takes every Unicode digit), rather than answered for other text. Messages that quote a String keep its units, and Objects.requireNonNull's message is the very String given. Machine::str_of keeps its signature, now for readers; Machine::units_of is what a String is.

Reproducer first: lib/tests/values.rs, the values stream's model conformance test, runs 67 small String methods (lib/tests/fixtures/values/) on a real JVM and in the interpreter and requires the same code units, or a refusal where one is listed. Before the fix, 28 cases differed and one was refused; now all agree. The full lib suite passes (cargo test: 476 tests, the integration contract application_core.rs included). The audit of what native runs faithfully, two wrong answers found outside V1's core (Character's classification uses Rust's Unicode tables, and a surrogate char renders as U+FFFD in a contract), and an interface request for the merge (the class reader decodes a string literal lossily) are in the brief's Progress. Next: the own checker's bounded Strings.

commits.summary: application-core values V1 step 2: the own checker's Strings are bounded code units with content, and a String parameter has every content up to its bound
commits.body:
In the native engine (lib/src/bmc/), a String is now an object whose content is UTF-16 code units of a symbolic length, a char cell per unit it may have, any of the 65,536 values. The content reuses the arrays' machinery for merging, aliasing and witnesses, and Obj::content/as_array keep a String apart from an array. A literal has its units. length, isEmpty, charAt (StringIndexOutOfBoundsException), equals (identity, null, another class, then the lengths and every unit) and startsWith (NullPointerException on null) are modelled on content, through bmc::models_string_method, which the gap scan shares. A compiler-generated concatenation of Strings, null, chars and constants has its parts' content. A number concatenated gives a String with no content, whose methods stay the jdk-primitive-method gap. One that could pass bmc::MAX_STRING_CONTENT (64) units ends with a named limit wherever its content is asked for, never a truncated String. A harness String parameter is taken only under an explicit bound, the new bmc::Parameters::max_string_length; None refuses it by name. It has every content up to the bound, the same nullable and may-alias options as an array, and its witness is its code units in raw_arrays.

Reproducer: before, every String parameter was outside the fragment (bmc::unsupported_parameter), and String.length/charAt/equals were gaps. The new tests in lib/tests/values.rs run the checker on harness-shaped methods (lib/tests/fixtures/values/values/Checks.java), merging paths from the start and never. Every violation's witness is replayed on the JVM (ValuesRunner now takes String, null and same-object arguments) and in the interpreter, and must throw the check's AssertionError. The quote fixture's Codes.vip rewrite is proved up to 5 units, and its dropped-prefix defect refuted with 'VI' plus a unit that isn't 'P'. An isolated surrogate and 'A\\0' are found as inputs. A defect that takes a surrogate pair for one unit is refuted with the pair. Equal content behind distinct references refutes an identity claim. Further cases cover charAt's bounds, startsWith(null), null Strings, the bound (proved under 4, refuted with 5 units under 5), and concatenation up to the cap and past it. The gap scan counts the modelled methods as no gap. Evidence level: tested. The whole lib suite passes (lib unit 226, alignment 34, application_core 14, compare 1, conformance 10, effects 18, foundations 5, heap 49, integration 65, observations 12, skill 1, summaries 40, values 8).

commits.summary: application-core values V1 step 3: the String value adapter, its domain, evidence, witness reader, encoding and rebuilding
commits.body:
values::StringAdapter (lib/src/values.rs) is the String's value adapter: a spec::plans::ValueDomain of kind string with its bound, nullability and the model's evidence (values::string_model: the model identity STRING_MODEL, JDK 25.0.5 sampled, level tested, and what it leaves out), the bound for the own checker (bound, bmc::Parameters::max_string_length), a reader of a String argument from the checker's witness (read: units, null, or an earlier argument's object), and encode and rebuild between the interpreter's JStr and a witness's units. A String outside the domain (too long, null where not nullable, not code units) is refused by each, never cut. Verified by four unit tests and by lib/tests/values.rs, whose refutations now read their witnesses through read and rebuild every String in the interpreter's replay through rebuild, checked to encode back; the whole lib suite passes, the integration contract included (one untouched timing test of bmc::bits failed once under load and passed alone and on the rerun).

values::adapter still refuses a String, now saying the adapter is built and what a check lacks: the wiring that would let a regression or property check take a String parameter (the harness declaring it, the bound passed to the checker, jbmc::JbmcResult::arguments and the replay rebuilding it) is in the objects stream's files, and is recorded under Progress as an interface request. The briefs disagree here: the integration contract's V1 row (v1_a_symbolic_string_crosses_the_proof_boundary) accepts only the values stream's refusal, and the values brief makes V1's crossing of the proof boundary this stream's row, while the main brief's ownership gives harness/, equivalence.rs and property.rs to objects. Registering the adapter before that wiring would fail the contract's V1 row on another stream's files, so it waits for it.

commits.summary: application-core values V2 step 1: the own checker runs the immutable-list models, keeping order, duplicates and aliases (verification pending)
commits.body:
V2's audit, then its first step. The models in lib/models/java/util (List.of, List.copyOf, ImmutableCollections' List12, ListN, ListItr) are the JDK's lists step for step with no JDK call, but were marked JBMC only, so the tool's own checker met List.of as the gap jdk-static-method and no check reached a list. models::CHECKER_RUNS now lists them. The checker calls their static methods as application methods, runs ImmutableCollections' initializer and holds its statics (ClassPath::checker_class, the one empty list and a list of one's sentinel), and treats AbstractCollection()'s empty constructor as exact. The gap scan walks the same methods and counts an interface call on a list or its iterator as no gap where the models implement it (gaps::dispatched_to_models). Any other java.util collection the checker could hold is made by a JDK call that is a gap where it's made, so copyOf of an ArrayList is still refused by name.

Reproducer: lib/tests/values.rs runs the checker on harness-shaped methods (tests/fixtures/values/values/Lists.java) that make lists the way a harness would: List.of over 0 to 3 constructor-made lines, any two of which may be one object. Before this change all of them met the jdk-static-method gap. Now the basket fixture's three rewrites are proved. Its four defects are refuted: a duplicate skipped, the last line for the first, a copy for the element, and an alias between elements. So is a wrong claim that two elements are two lines. size, isEmpty and the iterator behave as the JDK's; get out of range throws the JDK's class (List12 IndexOutOfBounds, ListN ArrayIndexOutOfBounds); null elements and changes are refused; copyOf of such a list is the list itself. Every refutation is replayed on a JVM and in the interpreter. Evidence level: tested.

The conformance corpus changed. 12 of its list claims that had no own-checker verdict are now decided, each as the JVM decides it. Their records are updated and lib/benchmark/conformance.json is re-blessed. One assertion of tests/conformance.rs is narrowed: it read any claim that strict decides while advised stops on a gap as a scan seeing an unreachable gap. listCopyMutable's refutation is a violation on a path with no gap, which strict's documented rule lets stand, so the assertion now fails only on a strict proof that advised stops on. The corpus also found an interpreter bug: an immutable collection's iterator refused remove instead of throwing UnsupportedOperationException, so one witness didn't replay. That is fixed (Native::Iterator records whether its collection is immutable). Found but not fixed, under Progress: the interpreter names every immutable list ListN, so getClass of a List12 differs from the JVM's. The whole lib suite passes. Job 20261108-070211-application-core-values-v2-step-1-the-co runs the corpus's two JBMC tests (engine jbmc and auto, and auto --confirm, which now confirms the checker's list proofs). Expected to pass.

commits.summary: application-core values V2 step 2: the list value adapter, its domain and model digest, the harness's Java, witness reader, encoding and rebuilding
commits.body:
values::ListAdapter is the value adapter for one bounded immutable-list family: lists List.of makes over at most max_length (up to 10) objects of one application class, null among them where the domain says so. Its domain is the shared ValueDomain of kind list, with the model's evidence (values::list_model: the list models with the SHA-256 of their bytecode, values::list_model_digest, so that a change in a model changes the evidence's identity; level tested on JDK 25.0.5; what it leaves out). Since the own checker runs the list models (V2 step 1), a list needs no symbolic form: a harness makes one as an application would, by List.of over max_length objects it made by the construction plan, from int choices the checker is free in (ListAdapter::choices, admitted, java): null, the length, and for each element after the first which made object it is, so that every pattern of duplicates and aliases is a choice. ListAdapter::read gives the witness's list as the plan's nodes in order; encode and rebuild go between it and the interpreter's list through values::Nodes (ValueAdapter's methods now take the run's plan objects; a String ignores them), rebuilding by the interpreter's own List.of. A list outside the family, longer than the bound, holding an object the plan didn't make, or a list of Strings, is refused by name, never cut or copied in.

Verified by five unit tests in values.rs and a new end-to-end test in lib/tests/values.rs, which generates a harness-shaped class from the adapter's own Java over the basket's kernels, runs the own checker on it (merging from the start and never), proves total, first (identity), clearAll and a nullable total, and refutes a skipped duplicate, a reordering, a copy for the element, an alias between mutable elements and a nullable domain's null. Each witness is read through the adapter and replayed on the JVM and, through the adapter's rebuilt lists, in the interpreter, which must observe the difference; each rebuilt list encodes back as its witness. Sabotaging the adapter's picks makes the test fail. The whole lib suite passes. Evidence level tested; no job.

values::adapter still refuses a list parameter by name: making it in a harness and rebuilding it in the replay is the objects stream's wiring, recorded under the brief's Progress as an interface request, with two points for the merge (a bound for String elements in the shared ElementKind, and the frozen basket claims' model evidence, level modelled, differing from the adapter's).

commits.summary: application-core values V3 step 1: an evidence record per modelled String and list operation, checked against boundary cases on the JVM, the interpreter and the own checker
commits.body:
values::OPERATIONS holds one record (values::OperationEvidence) for each of the 14 operations the values models implement: for Strings the literal, the compiler's concatenation, length, isEmpty, charAt, equals and startsWith; for lists List.of's fixed forms, copyOf, size, isEmpty, get, the iterator's path, and the changes the lists refuse. Each record has its model family, what implements it in the own checker, the interpreter and for JBMC, the JDK it was sampled on (25.0.5), the inputs it admits, the exceptions it was seen to throw, what it leaves out, and its level, which is tested and never proved.

The new fixture lib/tests/fixtures/values/values/Operations.java has 86 boundary cases. lib/tests/values.rs runs each one on the JVM, in the interpreter, and in the own checker through a generated method that asserts the JVM's outcome: a String by its code units, an exception by its exact class. The test fails unless all three agree, unless the exceptions each record's cases throw are exactly the ones it lists, and unless every String method the checker models on content has a record. All three engines agreed on every case. Three sabotages each fail the test: a missing exception in a record, 42 wrong expected values, and the wrong exception class for a List12's get. The whole lib suite passes. Strict gap detection and the bound sweep are next.

commits.summary: application-core values V3 step 2: an operation outside the values models is a named gap under strict, never a verdict
commits.body:
V3's strict gap detection. String methods other than the five the own checker models on content were already named gaps; list methods were not. Since V2 step 1 the checker ran every method the immutable-list models implement, so claims over a list's equals, hashCode, toArray, addAll, remove(Object), sort and List.of's array form were proved on bytecode no evidence record samples, and contains/indexOf stopped at a gap inside the models rather than at the call. Each record of values::OPERATIONS now names its calls (OperationEvidence::calls). A call from outside the list models into them that no list record names (values::samples_list_call) is the JDK call it names, for the engine and the gap scan alike (bmc::gaps::outside_the_list_records): a gap of its kind, or a refusal for toArray's array result. The models' calls among themselves are unchanged. values::LIST_MODEL goes to 2, since the checker's list semantics changed. The engine's table, the scan's module docs, lib/models/README.md and lib/README.md say so.

Reproducer: lib/tests/values.rs's an_operation_outside_the_values_models_is_a_named_gap_under_strict runs 20 harness-shaped checks (tests/fixtures/values/values/Outside.java), each reaching one such operation with a claim the JVM upholds. Each must end, merging from the start and never, with no verdict and its gap named, and the scan must report the same gap without walking the models' unsampled methods. Before the fix, 37 of its 60 checks failed. A unit test holds each record's calls to the models and to the String methods the checker models. Removing the rule from the engine's dispatch fails the test (20 operations), and so does removing it from the scan's walk (11).

Workloads without Strings keep their results. The whole lib suite passes, and the benchmark's Python tests pass. Only four list claims of the conformance corpus change: they reach List.of's array form, and go back to the U they had before this stream (listNull's proof, both of listCopySame's, listOfArray's refutation). lib/benchmark/conformance.json is re-blessed. One corpus assertion is narrowed to a single named claim with its exact gaps (ADVISED_ON_EXCLUDED_PATHS). Strict still proves listChange under n == 0 || n == 8, since the engine prunes the paths to remove(Object) and addAll. --gaps advised decides from the static scan and stops on those two gaps: the scan's documented imprecision, not a wrong verdict. Evidence level unchanged (tested). No job: seconds, inline. Found, for review: the corpus samples the array form on the JVM, but no record does; a record would bring those four claims back if a fixture needed it.

commits.summary: application-core values: VF-023's diagnosis, why JBMC refutes that a one-element List.of has size 1 (verification pending)
commits.body:
V2 step 1's job 20261108-070211-… failed at its auto --confirm step (VF-023 in verification/findings.md). JBMC 6.11.0 refutes the corpus's listSizes(n=1) and listChange(n=0), which the own checker proves and the JVM, the interpreter and lib/models' lists run on a JVM all hold, so JBMC's verdict is the wrong one. Both witnesses are a one-element List.of. Its List12 keeps the static sentinel ImmutableCollections.EMPTY as its second element, and size() compares against it. Every other list claim JBMC decides agrees with the JVM. Nothing is changed before the cause is shown: the item has one timebox attempt left.

Job 20261108-082244-vf-023-s-diagnosis-why-jbmc-refutes-that runs verification/triage/vf023.sh: three property proofs under JBMC alone with their logs kept. They are a one-element list's size, the same after List.of() has initialized ImmutableCollections, and a two-element control (1, 1 and 2 on the JVM, checked inline). The script extracts the trace's assignments to EMPTY, e1 and the class-initialization flags. The stream brief's Progress records the triage and the next step.

commits.summary: application-core values: the tiny bound sweep finds no String cliff up to 64 units and a list cliff at 6 to 7 elements; VF-023's probes refute the class-initialization guess
commits.body:
lib/tests/values.rs's a_tiny_sweep_over_the_string_and_list_bounds runs the own checker on one correct check and one planted defect per family, at a few bounds, under both search orders, and prints the times (the verdicts are asserted, the times never). Strings: vipRewritten proved, vipShortened refuted and equalsByUnits proved at bounds 1 to 64 (the content cap), each in 0.07 s or less. A check that loops over a String's units itself needs an unwinding bound past the String's; under the default --unwind 16 a 32-unit bound is the named unwinding limit, which the test asserts. Lists, through the list adapter's own Java: the basket's total proved and its duplicate-skipping defect refuted over lists of 1 to 5 lines in the suite (8 s for the whole file in the dev profile). Past that there is a cliff inside the adapter's bound of 10: 345 paths for 5 lines, 1,833 for 6 (4 s release, 40 s dev), and 7 lines do not finish. The cost is paths, not solving: the adapter's picks are n! alias patterns, each a chain of conditionals the checker forks on. Lists of 6, 7, 8 and 10 lines are the ignored reproducer the_list_sweep_past_five_lines, which fails today. Also found: the checker's 20 s time limit ended at 138 s, since the deadline is read every 256 steps.

VF-023's diagnosis job 20261108-082244-vf-023-s-diagnosis-why-jbmc-refutes-that passed: JBMC proves a one-element List.of's size 1, with or without List.of() first, so the class-initialization order is not the cause and the models are unchanged. The corpus's claims differ from the probes in choosing between lists of different classes, which the next probe isolates. No timebox attempt was spent. The brief's Progress records both, and what comes next.

commits.summary: application-core values: VF-023's second probe, nine JBMC proofs that isolate which ingredient of listSizes and listChange makes JBMC refute a one-element list's size (verification pending)
commits.body: The first probe showed JBMC proving a one-element List.of's size alone, so class initialization order is not VF-023's cause. verification/triage/vf023-choice.sh now runs the corpus's own two claims under JBMC alone, which must reproduce the refutation, then seven reductions, one ingredient each: a choice between two List12s, a List12 or a ListN, EMPTY_LIST or a List12, the assumption alone, objects made first, listChange's choice without its switch, and its switch without the choice. For each refutation it keeps JBMC's failed property and the trace steps that touch the lists. Checked inline: the script's JVM part (every claim holds for n from -2 to 12, and listSizes(1..3) and listChange(0, 8) give 10 20 30 and 1 1), its trace extractor on a made-up JBMC log, and the own checker proving all nine claims. Nothing in the models changes before the result.

commits.summary: application-core values: the list cliff past five lines fixed, an array's cell holds a symbolic reference of its element type, so List.of's varargs array no longer splits a path per pick
commits.body:
The tiny bound sweep found that the own checker couldn't check lists of 7 or more lines within its time limit (6 took 4 s, 1,833 paths). The cause was not the list adapter's encoding but the checker's aastore. List.of of three or more elements builds a varargs array, and an array's cell could hold only a known object, so storing each pick (a symbolic reference among the made objects) split the path per object it may be: n! paths for n elements. Now a cell of an array of references holds a symbolic reference as a field does (bmc::Array::refs holds Vals), stored as it is when every object it may be is of the array's element type. Any other store still splits per object, so a store the JVM refuses with ArrayStoreException is refused by name as before. Merging chooses between two paths' cells, and a path that takes one option of a reference substitutes it in cells too.

The ignored reproducer the_list_sweep_past_five_lines (6, 7, 8 and 10 lines) passed: 6 lines in 0.03 s, 7 in 1.4 s, 8 in 2.7 s, 10 in 12.8 s (908 paths, release, merging from the start), so the suite's sweep in lib/tests/values.rs now covers every length up to the adapter's bound of 10 and the ignored test is gone. A new test, an_array_cell_holds_a_symbolic_reference_of_its_element_type, checks three new checks in lib/tests/fixtures/values/values/Lists.java: a reference read back from a cell is the one stored (proved), a claim that it is the first line is refuted and replayed on the JVM and in the interpreter, and a choice between a Line and a String stored into a Line[] is refused naming the ArrayStoreException, under both search orders. Verified by the whole library suite in the dev profile, 15 suites all passing (the release build of the unit tests is killed for memory in the 4 GB scope while linking with LTO). values::LIST_MODEL is not bumped: what the checker computes is unchanged, only how many paths it takes. lib/README.md's description of the checker's fragment ('cells hold objects or null') is a shared page and is left for the merge, recorded under the brief's Progress. No job: no JBMC, and the sweep runs in 36 s inline.

commits.summary: application-core values: VF-023's second probe names the ingredient, a choice between two lists; its third probe tests whether the model List re-declaring Collection's methods fixes JBMC's dispatch of size() (verification pending)
commits.body:
VF-023's second probe (job 20261108-091002-..., passed) shows JBMC 6.11.0 refuting l.size() whenever l is one of two lists made on different branches, whatever their classes (even two List12s), while proving it for a single list. Its trace of oneOrTwo(n=1) shows JBMC calling ImmutableCollections$ListN.size on a List12, which returns 0, and every refuted probe reaches java.util.List.size() as JBMC's stub. The model java.util.List declares List's own abstract methods but not those it inherits from Collection, which is not on JBMC's class path; the JDK's List re-declares them, and every list claim JBMC got right asks a declared method or has a single list.

The third probe, verification/triage/vf023-dispatch.sh, tests that without changing the repository: six JBMC proofs (the corpus's listSizes and listChange, oneOrTwo, oneOrThree, emptyOrOne, and oneAssumed as the control) under the tool's models as they are and under a patched copy whose List re-declares Collection's 15 abstract methods, put first on JBMC's class path, keeping each probe's goto dispatch of size(). Checked inline: the JVM outcomes, the patched models compiling and declaring size/isEmpty/iterator. No fix, so no timebox attempt is spent. Progress in llm-dlc/loops/application-core-values.md records the result and the next step.

commits.summary: application-core values V3 step 3: a claim's String and list domains are resolved under this tool's models, so a change of model identity or bound changes exactly the claims it affects; VF-023's third probe refutes the declaration hypothesis
commits.body:
values::resolve (with values::ValueModels) turns a claim's stated value domain into the one the check runs and the claim key digests: its kind, nullability and bound as stated, with the model's own evidence (STRING_MODEL, or LIST_MODEL with the list models' bytecode SHA-256), and refuses by name a claim stated under another model identity, another JDK, a stronger evidence level than the model has, or a domain the adapters refuse. Before, the frozen claims' placeholder words for the model were digested as written, so a model change reached no claim key except through the binary's digest. Verified by two unit tests and tests/values.rs's a_change_of_value_model_or_bound_changes_exactly_the_claims_it_affects over the 8 frozen claims (a list model change changes exactly the basket claims, a String model change exactly the quote family's, a lower bound every claim with a value domain, never one key for two claims, a stale claim refused); sabotaging resolve fails it; the whole lib suite passes in the dev profile. Wiring resolve into construction::check_plans and proof_cache is an interface request for the merge (other streams' files).

VF-023's third probe (job 20261108-093809-vf-023-s-third-probe-does-the-model-java, passed at b5fd6e15) refutes the hypothesis that the model java.util.List's missing Collection declarations cause JBMC's wrong size(): with them declared JBMC refutes the same five probes, and its class-identifier dispatch is the same and correct in both, so JBMC misreads the class of a reference to one of two objects. Nothing changed on it; one timebox attempt is left, and Progress names the choice. Also recorded for review: in that probe's declared variant the tool printed 'Property violated' on a witness its replay could not run (objects stream's property.rs).

commits.summary: application-core values: VF-023 decided, no fix in the values stream's files; a reproducer for the merge's change to equivalence::confirm, which would take a JBMC refutation through a stub that doesn't reproduce for no verdict
commits.body:
VF-023 (the corpus's listSizes and listChange under --engine auto --confirm): the evidence in hand refutes the last candidate fix in lib/models, a model where every immutable list is one class. The probe oneOrTwo chooses between two List12s, one class, and stock JBMC 6.11.0 refutes it all the same; its dispatch of size() falls back to java.util.List.size()'s stub on a reference to one of two objects. That is JBMC's symbolic execution, external work the main brief defers, and the tool's outcome is sound (neither verdict stands). The timebox's last attempt is not spent on it.

What would close the entry is in the objects stream's equivalence::confirm: a JBMC refutation that doesn't reproduce in the interpreter, and whose program reaches a stub, is no verdict. confirm already applies that rule to a refutation through a jbmc_gaps::Defect, and jbmc_gaps::hold applies it to a JBMC proof through a stub. The new test confirm_takes_a_refutation_through_a_jbmc_stub_that_does_not_reproduce_for_no_verdict (tests/values.rs, #[ignore]d, with the fixture values.Choice#oneOrTwo) runs it against a stand-in JBMC whose program reaches the stub and whose answer is the real one's (n=1). Today it fails with the corpus's message. With the rule patched into confirm (in the working copy only, then reverted) it passes: the proof stands, not confirmed, naming java.util.List.size(). The interface request is recorded under the brief's Progress.
